title: Federal Register: Improving Protections for Workers in Temporary Agricultural Employment in the United States, final rule (DOL)

history.reason: Source read directly on the access date; findings transcribed from the document.

publisher: U.S. Department of Labor (via GovInfo / Federal Register)
source_type: Government final rule with regulatory flexibility analysis and summarized public comments
reliability: Government document; the issuing agency is also the party imposing or administering the requirement. Contains industry commenters' counter-claims.
findings: In DOL's small-entity analysis, of 9,927 H-2A employers, DOL obtained revenue and employee data matches for 2,615 employers in FY 2020 and FY 2021 certification data.
Of those 2,615, DOL determined 2,159 were small (82.5 percent); these unique small entities averaged 11 employees and about $3.6 million in annual revenue.

A commenter (AmericanHort) argued DOL's burden estimate was "drastically low" and a "gross underestimation", characterizing DOL's proposal as estimating a one-time $54.00 familiarization cost and $108.00 to complete the new application with owner, manager and supervisor information for small businesses.
Employers must submit job orders and applications on Forms ETA-790/790A and ETA-9142A with required addenda.
limitations: DOL's final per-employer burden figures were not extracted; the $54 and $108 numbers are a commenter's characterization of the proposal.
Later changes to the rule (several H-2 related rules appeared in searches) were not read.
